reading: The 7x7 input is noise dominated by one colour (1, 2 or 3). The output is a fixed 3x3 glyph of colour 8 chosen by that dominant colour: 1 -> [008,880,080], 2 -> [000,888,000], 3 -> [088,080,080].

slots.feature: most common non-background colour of the input
slots.lookup: learned table dominant colour -> fixed 3x3 colour-8 glyph (1: 008/880/080, 2: 000/888/000, 3: 088/080/080)

why: every pair's output equals the glyph for its input's majority non-zero colour

reading: Every isolated single cell gets a 3x3 square ring around it, and the ring colour depends on the centre colour (3 -> 6, 8 -> 4, 2 -> 1).

slots.shape: the 8 neighbours of the anchor (3x3 ring)

why: each marker's 8 neighbours take the mapped colour; the marker cell itself stays; all other cells unchanged

reading: The 3x3 input is tiled into an N x N block grid where N is the number of background cells; the first K blocks in reading order get a copy of the input, K being the number of foreground cells; the rest stay empty.
why: every 3x3 block of the output is either the input or all background; copies count = fg pixel count, filled row-major; output side = 3 x bg count
invariants: each copy identical to the input

reading: Each input cell is enlarged to a 3x3 block of its colour (scale by 3).
why: output cell (y,x) equals input cell (y//3, x//3) on every pair

reading: Four colour-5 marker cells (top, bottom, left, right) bound a box; a rectangle outline in the colour of the hollow shape is drawn one cell inside the markers.

slots.bounds: rows from topmost marker+1 to bottommost marker-1, columns from leftmost marker+1 to rightmost marker-1

why: the outline cells lie exactly one step inside each marker; nothing else changes

reading: A lattice of separator lines splits the grid into equal cells; one cell holds a pattern. The pattern is copied into every cell whose cell-row and cell-column differ from the source cell's by an even number.

slots.unit: the one non-empty lattice cell's contents
slots.targets: lattice cells at (r0+2i, c0+2j) for all i,j in range
slots.lattice: full rows/columns of the separator colour

why: every cell with the source's cell-index parity in both directions equals the source pattern; others remain empty

reading: A key row above a separator lists colours k0,k1,k2,...; around the single marker below, concentric square rings are drawn: the centre keeps k0 and the ring at Chebyshev distance d gets colour k_d (colour 0 rings stay background).

slots.centre: the single cell below the separator
slots.key: row 0 colours left to right (index = ring distance)
slots.rings: cells at Chebyshev distance d from centre, d = 1..len(key)-1, clipped to the area below the separator

why: every cell below the separator at distance d < len(key) has colour key[d]
invariants: key row (pair 0 also changes one key cell 8->5, a quirk not explained)

reading: A 2x2 block of four colours sits in the grid; at each of its four diagonal corners a 2x2 block is drawn in the colour of the diagonally opposite cell of the block (clipped at the border).

slots.targets: 2x2 areas diagonally adjacent to each block corner
slots.colour: the block cell diagonally opposite that corner

why: top-left target = bottom-right colour, top-right = bottom-left, bottom-left = top-right, bottom-right = top-left

reading: Each box marked by four corner brackets contains some 1-cells in one half; that half is mirrored across the box's centre line (along its long side) so the content is symmetric, and all stray 1-cells outside the boxes are erased.

slots.frames: boxes outlined by four L-shaped corner brackets of one colour
slots.axis: the box's centre line across its long dimension

why: inside every box the content is mirror-symmetric about its centre line; no colour-1 cell remains outside boxes

reading: Full lines of colour 5 cut the grid into cells; the top-left cell is filled with 1, the middle cell (middle cell-row and middle cell-column) with 2, and the bottom-right cell with 3.

slots.cells: panels of the lattice cut by full separator lines
slots.targets: first cell -> 1, central cell (middle index of cell-rows and of cell-columns) -> 2, last cell -> 3

why: exactly those three lattice cells become solid colour 1, 2, 3; nothing else changes
